title: Asian Stocks Under Pressure After US Tech Selloff: Markets Wrap
summary: Asian stocks were set for broad declines Tuesday after a tech-led selloff on Wall Street outweighed a drop in oil, as traders weighed Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s plan to isolate Iran from the global economy.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 25
summary: Oil held a decline as the US ramped up economic pressure on Iran and its trading partners in a bid to force the resumption of energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Bond Investor Ed Al-Hussainy on Bessent's Treasury Twist
summary: Ed Al-Hussainy, Portfolio Manager at Columbia Threadneedle Investments, discusses the relative stability of the U.S. dollar against developed market currencies, while highlighting the strength of emerging market currencies fueled by carry trades supported by higher real yields in countries like Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, and South Africa. Despite strong U.S. economic fundamentals, including low unemployment and steady growth, the dollar has underperformed, partly due to the Federal Reserve's slower rate repricing compared to other central banks. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump's Family Seeking National Bank Charter
summary: Donald Trump's family has won preliminary approval to start a national bank, riding a wave of deregulation under the Trump administration. For the president’s family, the goal is to expand the use of USD1, their dollar-backed stablecoin, World Liberty Financial said earlier this month after receiving conditional approval. Bloomberg News Financial Reporter Paige Smith has the details of the move for today's Big Take. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hartree's Morse: 3 Things Define Hormuz Strait's Future
summary: Ed Morse, Senior Advisor and Commodities Analyst, discusses the recent fall in Brent crude oil prices. The decline is attributed to market attention on the potential impact of Iran sanctions, which are influencing supply expectations and investor sentiment in the commodities market. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Copy Trading Offers Alternative to Traditional Investing
summary: Steven Wang, Founder & CEO of Dub, launched the copy trading platform 3 years ago after dropping out of Harvard to become an entrepreneur. He says the app offers a unique alternative to sports betting, and fresh opportunities for the increasing number of young Americans who say they are now investing their money to grow try and grow their wealth. Wang says Dub is for great traders who "don't need to go the traditional sort of boys club and Wall Street path to really become the next superstar." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bilt CEO, Equinox Exec. Chairman on New Partnership
summary: The segment features a discussion with Ankur Jain, CEO of BILT, and Harvey Spevak, Equinox Group Executive Chairman, about the newly launched exclusive partnership between Bilt, a membership and hospitality platform, and Equinox, a luxury fitness brand. The collaboration aims to connect the audiences of both brands by allowing Bilt members to redeem Bilt cash for credits that can be used toward Equinox experiences. The two speak with Romaine Bostick & Emily Graffeo on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ontario's Ford Says Standing Up to Trump Won't Be Easy
summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says standing up to President Donald Trump in this trade war won't be easy. Ford says Canada must be willing to escalate this trade war and every option should be on the table.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Canadian Stocks Rise Despite Breakdown in US Trade Talks
summary: Canadian stocks ended the day higher, thanks largely to gains from precious metals miners, after the collapse of talks with the US unleashed what threatens to become a widening trade war.

title: Strategy Sets Up Reserve That Can Be Used to Buy Bitcoin
summary: Michael Saylor’s Strategy Inc. is adding a new pool of cash to its balance-sheet toolkit, part of an effort to preserve flexibility as its once-powerful financing model remains under pressure.

title: Treasury Buybacks Are a 'Cloud' Over Markets, Apollo's Slok Says
summary: Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok comments on the economic impact of the the US Treasury's strategic debt buyback operations. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Slok also discusses the outlook for Federal Reserve monetary policy. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: UK Power Equipment Rental Firm Aggreko Files for New York IPO
summary: Aggreko Plc filed for a US initial public offering, revealing the private equity-backed power equipment rental company turned profitable as revenue increased.

title: Stocks Fall as Chip Rout Overshadows Drop in Oil: Markets Wrap
summary: Wall Street kicked off the week on a cautious note, with a selloff in chipmakers outweighing an oil drop as traders parsed Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s plan to isolate Iran from the global economy.

title: Guggenheim's Walsh Says Firm Is Cooperating With Regulators
summary: Anne Walsh, chief investment officer of Guggenheim Partners, says the asset management firm is fully cooperating with regulators as they investigate an accounting issue at one of its subsidiaries. US prosecutors are looking at Mark Walter's investment empire and his relationship with Guggenheim. Walsh says Guggenheim's investment or trade-allocation processes are not part of the probe. She speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Expands Search for Critical-Mineral Projects for Defense Gear
summary: The Trump administration is seeking investment pitches from domestic producers of metals used in fighter jets, night-vision goggles and tank armor.

title: Tech Leads US Stocks Lower as Nvidia Earnings, Jackson Hole Loom
summary: Technology names led a decline in US stocks on Monday as investors geared up for a busy week of economic data and earnings from Nvidia Corp.

title: Nvidia Slides Ahead of Earnings as Tech Stocks Retreat | Closing Bell
summary: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Emily Graffeo, Norah Mulinda and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Test Your ETF Knowledge In Our IQ Test
summary: Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu puts Isabelle Lee, Athanasios Psarofagis, and Eric Balchunas to the test on "Bloomberg ETF IQ" in this week's edition of "IQ Test." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Who Is Buying America’s Debt These Days?
summary: With the US now $40 trillion in the red, the US Treasury’s sudden move to rein in bond yields has cast a spotlight on who is, and isn’t, purchasing American debt these days. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: First Brands Bankruptcy-Payout Plan Rejected by Federal Judge
summary: A federal judge rejected the bankruptcy-payout plan of defunct auto-parts maker First Brands, concluding the proposal to raise money by suing a long list of insiders and business partners was not realistic.
